activities.anchor: the formal definition undersells the variety
activities.caption: file each fact under its belt
activities.name: ffBeltsSort

config.prompt: Three great belts — file each fact:

items.label: pine, spruce, fir and birch across Scandinavia, Russia, Alaska and Canada
holds roughly a third of all the trees on Earth
the richest soils and the wood industries' historic centres
the conifer rainforests of the Pacific Northwest
Amazonia, the Congo basin and Southeast Asia
holds most of the world's forest biodiversity and carbon

config.why: Tree canopy over 10% of the ground and more than half a hectare makes a forest by the FAO's working definition — but the belts differ wildly in species, soils and architecture.

activities.caption: pair each boreal trait with its job
activities.name: ffBorealMatch

config.prompt: The conifer belt's toolkit — pair each trait with what it does:

pairs.right: a head start on spring growth instead of rebuilding foliage each year
nutrients recycled tightly through a mat of undecayed litter and fungal partners on the roots

config.why: Slow-growing, fire-shaped, and covering huge continuous areas — the boreal belt is a study in making the most of a brief growing window.

activities.anchor: may wait decades for a light gap
activities.caption: call the emergents' height
activities.name: ffEmergentEstimate

config.prompt: In the humid rainforest, solitary trees break clean above the continuous canopy. Roughly how tall do those emergents grow?
config.why: Above 50 metres — with the canopy below shading the floor so deeply that undergrowth is often surprisingly sparse, and woody lianas and epiphytes climbing the scaffolding.

activities.anchor: depends entirely on what it replaced
activities.caption: the plantation verdict, argued properly
activities.name: ffPlantationBranch

config.root: A country plants even-aged pines across a million hectares. The argument starts.

choices.label: No — a crop in rows
choices.feedback: By definition it is one: tree canopy over 10% of the ground, above half a hectare. Being a forest settles nothing.

choices.label: Yes — trees, therefore forest, therefore good
choices.feedback: It stores carbon and produces fibre efficiently, but supports far less biodiversity — and a dark, dense, single-species canopy often means less water regulation than a natural stand.

end.text: The verdict hangs on what stood before and what the stand is for.

config.why: The honest unit of judgement is the value ledger, not the tree count.

activities.anchor: The idea arrived as an emergency response
activities.caption: line up the sustained-yield arc
activities.name: ffSustainedOrder

config.prompt: From timber crisis to certification — sequence the founding idea's career:
items: 1713 — Carlowitz's Sylvicultura oeconomica: the first written statement that harvest must respect regrowth
the normal forest — Hartig's age classes in equal areas, yielding an even annual cut
exported worldwide — British India's forest departments (1860s), the US Forest Service (1905)
multiple use — the US Multiple-Use Sustained-Yield Act (1960)
certification and carbon accounting — FSC (1993), PEFC
config.why: The export carried a politics — European state forestry often criminalised long-established local uses — and the arc runs alarm → accounting → science → negotiation, the stage where forestry now lives.

activities.anchor: green credentials are real but conditional
activities.caption: true or false — reading the ledger rows
activities.name: ffLedgerJudge

statements.s: Harvesting trees automatically earns the climate credit, whatever happens to the regrowth.
statements.why: Only regrowth (or clearly growing stocks) earns that credit — wood substitutes for steel and concrete, but conditionally.

statements.s: New York drinks from managed forest watersheds — filtration for free, provided the catchment stays wooded.
statements.why: Water regulation is why so many great cities drink from protected forests.

statements.s: To a beetle or a warbler, clearcut, shelterwood and selection mean catastrophe, compromise and continuity.
statements.why: Biodiversity habitat makes every forestry decision a conservation decision — forests hold the majority of terrestrial species.

statements.s: Deforestation transfers roughly 10–12% of anthropogenic emissions back to the atmosphere in recent accounting years.
statements.why: Climate services cut both ways: standing forest stores carbon, clearing releases it.

activities.anchor: the tonnage matters more than the place
activities.caption: drag the divider — slogan vs ledger
activities.name: ffPlantingCompare

config.prompt: 'Planting trees is automatically good for the climate' — drag the divider:

before.label: The slogan
before.text: Trees absorb carbon, so more trees must mean less carbon — count the trees planted and relax.

after.label: The ledger
after.text: Afforesting natural grasslands or peatlands can release more carbon than it stores and destroy existing habitat; restoring degraded forest land is among the best climate instruments available.

config.why: A monoculture plantation and a restored mixed forest can carry identical 'trees planted' counts while sitting at opposite ends of the value ledger — where and how decides nearly everything.

activities.anchor: Silvicultural systems are the craft's core vocabulary
activities.caption: find the faulty line — three cutting methods
activities.name: ffCuttingSpot

config.prompt: One line of this cutting-methods note is wrong — click it:
lines: Clearcutting removes all trees — it suits shade-intolerant, even-aged species like pines, at maximum ecological cost.
Shelterwood leaves seed trees standing through regeneration, then removes them.
Selection harvests individual trees or small groups, keeping continuous uneven-aged cover.
Selection is the near-natural option — and demands the least skill of the three.
A managed forest is still an ecosystem, run on sunlight and soil.
config.correction: Selection demands the most skill of the three systems.
config.why: Clearcut, shelterwood and selection are the core vocabulary — and the near-natural one asks the most of the forester who keeps the cover continuous.
